d.g: A member of the second-highest of the four castes or varnas in traditional Hindu society: the warrior or military caste.
d.x: "Bṛhannaḍā said, 'It is not the habit of a kṣatriya to flee like this; death in battle is preferable to flight in fear.'" (Mahābhārata: "Virāṭa Parva")

kshatriya.e: From Sanskrit क्षत्रिय (kṣatriya, “(the warrior or military caste or a member of this caste”), from क्षत्र (kṣatra, “rule, dominion, authority”). Akin to satrap.

kshetra.e: Borrowed from Sanskrit क्षेत्र (kṣetra, “field, area, tract of land”).

d.g: A town in Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima, Morocco.

Ksar es-Seghir.e: Borrowed from French Ksar es-Seghir, from Moroccan Arabic القصر الصغير (le-qṣar le-ṣḡīr, le-qṣar eṣ-ṣḡīr), from Arabic القَصْر الصَّغِير (al-qaṣr aṣ-ṣaḡīr).

d.g: A city in Tangier-Tetouan-Al Hoceima, Morocco.

Ksar el-Kebir.e: Borrowed from French Ksar el Kébir, from Moroccan Arabic القصر الكبير (le-qṣar le-kbīr), from Arabic القَصْر الكَبِير (al-qaṣr al-kabīr).
